title: starter-impl-frames-hosted-api-developer-playbook
content:
Purpose: quick, implementation-forward messaging frames and testable pricing copy for the hosted endpoints product.

Audience: backend/frontend engineers, infra/platform leads who evaluate APIs during integration. Primary goal: make an engineer able to go from zero to a real request in <10 minutes, and remove billing friction for early experimentation. Secondary goal: provide succinct counters to common procurement/security concerns so SEs and platform partners can escalate with confidence.

Topline positioning (one-liner options to A/B test)
- Option A: "A hosted inference API that feels like a library: fast tokens, reliable latency, pay-for-what-you-build pricing."
- Option B: "Ship generative features without the ops burden — predictable performance, flexible routing, and per-route cost visibility."
- Option C: "The dev-first inference API: integrate in minutes, scale without surprises."

Developer-first value props (short bullets, for hero + callouts)
- Instant dev loop: SDKs that mirror common ecosystems (npm/python/ruby) + a playground with live token estimator.
- Predictable latency: curated model profiles and regional routing keep p95 latency consistent across loads.
- Debugable outputs: request-level tracing, token-level cost breakdown, and sample-preserving traces for reproducing failures.
- Low-start friction pricing: free test credits, burst credits for new projects, and a predictable PAYG baseline once you go live.
- Safe defaults: sandbox keys, request quotas, and tenant isolation so teams can trial without noisy blast radius.

Quickstart angles (3 microflows to test in UX & marketing)
1) "Hello endpoint" (60s microflow):
   - copy for CTA: "Try an example now — no account needed"
   - steps: open the sandbox playground -> paste prompt -> hit Run -> copy curl example -> paste locally
   - outcome: dev has a curl command and a sample to iterate in their repo.
2) "From snippet to route" (5–10 min flow):
   - copy for CTA: "Add a /summarize route in 5 minutes"
   - steps: npm install @redwood/inference -> import client -> small express/tinyhttp snippet -> attach env var -> send request -> basic logging example
   - outcome: working route with token-cost output and trace id shown in console.
3) "From POC to cost baseline" (15–30 min):
   - CTA: "Estimate monthly cost for your traffic pattern"
   - steps: run 50 sample requests through the estimator -> select recommended batching/quantization -> use projected pricing dashboard -> enable a sandbox commit to test burst capacity
   - outcome: team has a cost estimate and recommended config for next-stage trials.

Suggested microcopy for quickstart (concise, dev-facing)
- "Install the SDK, set REDWOOD_KEY, and make your first request."
- "Tokens used: 124 — estimated cost: $0.0037"
- "Preview responses streaming in 3 regions — choose where your data lives."
- Button labels: "Run in sandbox", "Copy curl", "Use this snippet"

Pricing language drafts (short web lines + FAQ snippets)
- Hero line: "Pay for tokens, not surprises — transparent per-token pricing with free trial credits."
- Billing detail line: "Metering is per prompt + completion token. Embeddings billed per vector unit. Volume discounts and reserved capacity available for high-throughput teams."
- Starter plan: "Free trial with $XX credits, then PAYG at $Y per 1k tokens (small volume tier). Includes 30-day request logs and standard rate limits."
- Transition language for Dedicated/Private: "When traffic grows, move to Dedicated for committed throughput and lower unit costs — migration preserves API compatibility and billing continuity."
- FAQ: "Do I pay for failed requests?" -> "Only requests that produce tokens are billed; client-side validation and short-circuiting prevents charges for malformed requests."
- FAQ: "What about hidden compute costs?" -> "We surface per-request latency and token breakdowns so teams can optimize prompts without guesswork."

Competitive notes (concise, tactical bullets we can feed to SEs)
- Large cloud AI endpoints: strength — integrated infra + enterprise billing; weakness — dev ergonomics and lack of transparent per-token cost breakdowns. Messaging: emphasize dev ergonomics and predictable unit economics.
- LLM API incumbents: strength — familiarity and large model catalog; weakness — limited operational controls for latency SLOs and complex routing. Messaging: talk about curated model profiles + routing policies that avoid surprise throttles.
- Inference infra vendors/self-hosted: strength — total control/cost at scale; weakness — ops burden and slow time-to-prototype. Messaging: tout ready-to-run hosted mode for early product velocity and a clear path to Dedicated/Private as needs change.

Objections + suggested SE responses (short scripts)
- "We already use cloud endpoints from our CSPs." -> "Those are great for raw access. Redwood focuses on predictable inference economics and developer-first controls (tracing, token breakdown, routing) so feature teams ship faster and debug cheaper."
- "Token billing is hard to forecast." -> "Our estimator + per-route dashboards translate requests into estimated monthly spend and recommended optimizations (batching, cache, model variant)."
- "We need compliance and data isolation." -> "Hosted works for many teams with VPC peering + contract controls; for regulated workloads, Private keeps the same API surface with customer-managed networking."

AB test ideas (copy to run in ads/onboarding)
- CTA A: "Try a live request" vs CTA B: "Estimate your monthly cost"
- Hero A: "Start in minutes" vs Hero B: "Predictable inference costs"
- Pricing copy length: short (one line) vs transparent (line + inline estimator)

Implementation notes for docs/console teams
- Surface the 3 quickstart flows as distinct cards (60s / 10min / 30min) with concrete outcomes.
- Include a small inline estimator on the quickstart page that accepts: avg tokens per request, qps, days per month -> returns projected spend and recommended config.
- Add a "why this route" tooltip explaining routing tiers (latency-first vs cost-first).

Open questions / things to validate with field teams
- Free credits amount — ops and finance input to finalize. Current placeholder: $100 credits for new teams.
- Default sandbox quotas — Ops to confirm safe limits for new orgs.
- Which SDK examples get promoted to hero snippets (node/python/go) — dev-ex picks preferred order.

Next steps (who does what)
- Marketing: convert hero lines into A/B tests for the landing page (Maya + Ethan).
- Docs: implement 3 quickstart cards + estimator widget (Priya).
- Product: finalize free credits and sandbox quotas (Samir + billing).

Notes to self: keep tone technical but approachable. Engineers should feel confident they can reproduce the flow locally and understand the cost implications in <15 minutes. Save longer, legal/compliance details for an enterprise-ready foldout rather than the primary quickstart.
